Source and timing notes

Dates and ordering. Timeline dates and times use Eastern time (America/New_York), labeled EDT or EST as applicable. Phone timestamps are interpreted using user-supplied America/New_York. Original archive times remain in source references. Equal-minute order does not establish sequence.

Conversation grouping. SMS blocks group consecutive records from the same source on the same day with gaps of no more than one hour; this is a display convention, not proof of a continuous discussion. An intervening source ends a block. Email blocks group adjacent same-subject records on the same day, ignoring Re/Fw prefixes; these are display groups, not verified reply threads.

Unknown times. Unknown-zone emails are listed separately and cannot be positioned reliably in the chronology.

Quoted content. Email content is an edited derivative, including shortened event records; quoted replies remain within their containing email. Quoted passages are not separate timeline events. Attribution follows quoted headers; quoted dates retain their original zone information and are not normalized when the zone is absent. Complete passages with matching quoted sender and time are collapsed with links to earlier records; new or conflicting headers and changed text stay visible. Display matching does not authenticate message identity. One-minute time discrepancies and name-only matches are noted at the affected quotations. Expanding history keeps duplicates collapsed; individual quotations can be opened.

Sources and attachments. Extracted email attachments are linked when available; other attachment names are references. Recognized signatures and routine footers are omitted from this reading view; archive text remains in Markdown; retain the original exports for unabridged source content. Consult the master Markdown, reference CSV, and original exports for verification. This compilation contains private and counsel correspondence.

Good morning So, the short answer is yes and no 😬 You can hire an attorney for the closing and to review everything. Most people don't, as it's just an added expense. In Indiana we use Title Companies to handle all the closing work (they have lawyers) so for the most part people don't hire attorneys. IF we were to split the land from 20 to 13 acres...yes, I would then say an attorney is needed. I would definitely have someone look over the easement for the lake/dock when we receive it before closing. For the rest of the transaction, however, an attorney is not needed. BUT you are more than welcome to hire/use one if you would like! I emailed another agent who is also a Real Estate Attorney but doesn't sell often, to see what he says. However, since it's the 4th, I may not get an answer today. Let me know if you have more questions. We can hop on a call as well. Thanks Darcy

RE: Purchase agreement and easement

▶Garrett Lawton → SamCc: Regina Gray, darcy@truebloodre.com
From: Garrett Lawton <glawton@mcneelylaw.com>To: Sam <samgpresnal@gmail.com>Cc: Regina Gray <graylregina@gmail.com>, "darcy@truebloodre.com" <darcy@truebloodre.com>
Here are some thoughts, and we can discuss more in a call. I’m available until around 5pm today and most of the day tomorrow. Just let me know on that. Also, happy to answer whatever questions these thoughts prompt. And please don’t take any of this to mean that I don’t think you should purchase this property. It looks great, but I’m just informing you of things to be aware of heading into this transaction to hopefully ease any points of frustration or confusion later. * Covenants -You’re effectively living under a traditional HOA with all the things that entails. Rather than flag each thing individually, I’d strongly encourage you to read the covenants so that you’re fully aware of each requirement, restriction, etc. Some of the most pressing in my mind are: * How is the board elected and how are ties in decisions broken, given that it seems likely the board will just have two people? The covenants explicitly state that this process is outlined in the bylaws, but apparently there aren’t any bylaws. * With architectural review, essentially anything you’ll want to do to the house or lot will require approval. This includes changes to the home itself (painting, additions, etc.). * I would ask for approval documents on anything build after 2009, when the covenants went into effect. * I would also ask for a letter from the HOA stating that the property is in good standing and there are no outstanding violations or unpaid assessments. * Purchase agreement/addendum * Paragraph H(1), I would change that $0 amount to match what is on the post-closing amendment. * You’ll want that easement agreement asap. You’d hate to get all the way to the week of closing only to find out that there’s something in the easement agreement that they won’t budge on. But if the agreement is to benefit the neighbor, they should be flexible on this. * Nothing to note on the addendum. * Easement * Darcy’s recommended surveyor said that he can work up the easement based on the plat. When I spoke with you earlier, I wasn’t aware that a plat existed, so I trust him on this. That said, I’d like to review that agreement once it is created. * Things to consider in the easement agreement: * What type of access exactly is being granted? This language should be specific. * Who is responsible for maintenance to things like docks, roads, paths, etc.? * Can the easement be revoked/changed, and if so, how? * Is this easement going to the property owners for the duration of their lives or running with their property? Assuming this is for the benefit of the neighbors. * Insurance/liability considerations. * Potential limitation on users/guests.

On Tue, Jul 7, 2026 at 3:36 PM Garrett Lawton <glawton@mcneelylaw.com<mailto:glawton@mcneelylaw.com>> wrote: Here are some thoughts, and we can discuss more in a call. I’m available until around 5pm today and most of the day tomorrow. Just let me know on that. Also, happy to answer whatever questions these thoughts prompt. And please don’t take any of this to mean that I don’t think you should purchase this property. It looks great, but I’m just informing you of things to be aware of heading into this transaction to hopefully ease any points of frustration or confusion later. * Covenants -You’re effectively living under a traditional HOA with all the things that entails. Rather than flag each thing individually, I’d strongly encourage you to read the covenants so that you’re fully aware of each requirement, restriction, etc. Some of the most pressing in my mind are: * How is the board elected and how are ties in decisions broken, given that it seems likely the board will just have two people? The covenants explicitly state that this process is outlined in the bylaws, but apparently there aren’t any bylaws. * With architectural review, essentially anything you’ll want to do to the house or lot will require approval. This includes changes to the home itself (painting, additions, etc.). * I would ask for approval documents on anything build after 2009, when the covenants went into effect. * I would also ask for a letter from the HOA stating that the property is in good standing and there are no outstanding violations or unpaid assessments. * Purchase agreement/addendum * Paragraph H(1), I would change that $0 amount to match what is on the post-closing amendment. * You’ll want that easement agreement asap. You’d hate to get all the way to the week of closing only to find out that there’s something in the easement agreement that they won’t budge on. But if the agreement is to benefit the neighbor, they should be flexible on this. * Nothing to note on the addendum. * Easement * Darcy’s recommended surveyor said that he can work up the easement based on the plat. When I spoke with you earlier, I wasn’t aware that a plat existed, so I trust him on this. That said, I’d like to review that agreement once it is created. * Things to consider in the easement agreement: * What type of access exactly is being granted? This language should be specific. * Who is responsible for maintenance to things like docks, roads, paths, etc.? * Can the easement be revoked/changed, and if so, how? * Is this easement going to the property owners for the duration of their lives or running with their property? Assuming this is for the benefit of the neighbors. * Insurance/liability considerations. * Potential limitation on users/guests.

From: Garrett Lawton <glawton@mcneelylaw.com>To: Sam <samgpresnal@gmail.com>Cc: Darcy Knott <darcy@truebloodre.com>, Regina Gray <graylregina@gmail.com>
Good afternoon, I would not advise agreeing to an easement before you’ve seen it. If it simply cannot be prepared prior to closing, I would advise not making the sale contingent on the easement, and then you could just grant one after you’ve purchased the property. Obviously, this means you’re not obligated to grant an easement at all, but I think that’s a fair trade for the sellers to make if they can’t produce an easement document prior to close. Just FYI, I’m headed out of town for a few days. I will try to periodically check my emails but if you have anything pressing, just have Darcy shoot me a text and I will take a look. I’ll have time here and there to assist.

These claims have an interesting back story that ended up causing us to switch insurance companies. Claims 1. The 25K claim was because of a few bats that found their way into our attic. The claim paid to have all attic entry points to be sealed thus preventing any further "bat infestations". Bats are a protected and they require special care to remove them and prevent further entry. In addition to the work needed to seal the attic, the money was used to also remove any and all bat waste/insulation, disinfect and re-insulate areas affected in the attic. This was done in 9/2024, and we have had no further issues. 2. One of the water claims was actually not a claim at all, but one was due to the fact I called after hours with a question which triggered a claim to be created. Apparently if you call with questions during the day, you are forwarded to your agency where the questions are answered in an appropriate manner. If you happen to call the general number after work hours as soon as the phone is picked up, a claim is created automatically. Obviously, I had no idea this was the process as I have never had a claim prior. The reason I called back in 2021 is because we found a dried water stain below the master bathroom. We had lived in the home for about a year prior to the stain being noticed. It was not wet but I called to see if I needed to notify my insurance company of what we found so it could be documented for the future. This led to the "water claim" being filed. The next morning the claims adjusted called, and I realized a claim had actually been created without them telling me. I told the claims adjuster the same info I did to the person the night before, and the claim was closed. We later found out from the prior owners one of the children overflowed the shower one time leading to the staining and no further water issues have been noticed since. Just in case we professionally sealed the base to ensure there would be no future risks. 3. The 2nd "water clam" in 2023 was triggered when a contracting company was hired to remove a retaining wall from the back yard, redirecting water drainage away from the downstairs patio and install a new retaining wall for a future pool. My insurance company suggested and strongly encouraged I create a claim in case something developed in relation to water damage to patio area so it could be documented appropriately by them and us. This documentation would be used in a court situation if needed. Luckly, we ended up getting a new contractor who was able to redirect water away in an appropriate manner, and we have had no further drainage concerns since. In the end, I requested the claim being closed, and a claims adjuster was never dispatched, and no payouts were received as noted. Derrick and Sarah Hasenour ------------------------------ --

From: Sam <samgpresnal@gmail.com> Sent: Sunday, August 2, 2026 11:51 AM To: Leslie Appel Maher <LAppel@gregoryappel.com> Cc: Jessica Eye <JEye@gregoryappel.com> Subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] Insurance Quote - 5306 State Road 144, Greenwood, IN 46143 Good morning Leslie, The sellers got back to me. Below is there response to the claims. -------- Claims: 1. The 25K claim was because of a few bats that found their way into our attic. The claim paid to have all attic entry points to be sealed thus preventing any further "bat infestations". Bats are a protected and they require special care to remove them and prevent further entry. In addition to the work needed to seal the attic, the money was used to also remove any and all bat waste/insulation, disinfect and re-insulate areas affected in the attic. This was done in 9/2024, and we have had no further issues. 2. One of the water claims was actually not a claim at all, but one was due to the fact I called after hours with a question which triggered a claim to be created. Apparently if you call with questions during the day, you are forwarded to your agency where the questions are answered in an appropriate manner. If you happen to call the general number after work hours as soon as the phone is picked up, a claim is created automatically. Obviously, I had no idea this was the process as I have never had a claim prior. The reason I called back in 2021 is because we found a dried water stain below the master bathroom. We had lived in the home for about a year prior to the stain being noticed. It was not wet but I called to see if I needed to notify my insurance company of what we found so it could be documented for the future. This led to the "water claim" being filed. The next morning the claims adjusted called, and I realized a claim had actually been created without them telling me. I told the claims adjuster the same info I did to the person the night before, and the claim was closed. We later found out from the prior owners one of the children overflowed the shower one time leading to the staining and no further water issues have been noticed since. Just in case we professionally sealed the base to ensure there would be no future risks. 3. The 2nd "water clam" in 2023 was triggered when a contracting company was hired to remove a retaining wall from the back yard, redirecting water drainage away from the downstairs patio and install a new retaining wall for a future pool. My insurance company suggested and strongly encouraged I create a claim in case something developed in relation to water damage to patio area so it could be documented appropriately by them and us. This documentation would be used in a court situation if needed. Luckly, we ended up getting a new contractor who was able to redirect water away in an appropriate manner, and we have had no further drainage concerns since. In the end, I requested the claim being closed, and a claims adjuster was never dispatched, and no payouts were received as noted.

From: Regina Gray <graylregina@gmail.com>To: Darcy Knott <darcy@truebloodre.com>, Sam <samgpresnal@gmail.com>
*Hi Darcy,* *Below our three options we wish to provide to the seller. We only have one question regarding option 1. Is it ok to keep as is and ask for the 30k off even though current inspection estimates are adding up to 24k or should we make it 25k off? Other than that we are good to go with the following. * At this time, we are not comfortable proceeding with the purchase of the home at the original purchase price of *$2,500,000* while accepting the easement and before all inspection results and repair estimates have been received and reviewed. Based on the information currently available, we would like to present the following two options for the sellers’ consideration: Option 1: - *Purchase Price:* *$2,470,000* - *Easement:* Remains in place - *Closing Date:* *August 12* - *Inspection Contingency:* Subject to our review of the pending mold test results and a complete HVAC inspection and repair estimate The revised purchase price reflects approximately *$24,224.37* in estimated repairs related to the plumbing, roof, septic system, and electrical system. We have not yet received a complete HVAC inspection or an estimate for the repairs identified during the home inspection. Simply stating that the HVAC systems are currently operating properly is not an adequate inspection result. We are requesting a professional evaluation of the issues identified during the home inspection, along with written estimates for any recommended repairs or replacement. We are not comfortable proceeding at the original purchase price without fully understanding the condition of the HVAC systems and the potential costs involved, as HVAC repairs or replacement could exceed *$30,000*. We also expect to receive the mold inspection results tomorrow. Moving the closing date to *August 12* will provide adequate time to receive and review the mold results and obtain the requested HVAC evaluation and repair estimates before closing. We reserve the right to revisit and renegotiate the purchase price if either of the following occurs: - The mold test is positive and the estimated remediation is required - The estimated cost of HVAC repairs or replacement exceeds *$5,000*. Under this option, we would accept the easement and proceed at a purchase price of *$2,470,000*, subject to the inspection conditions stated above. Option 2: - *Purchase Price:* *$2,525,000* - *Easement:* Removed - *Property Condition:* Purchased as-is, with no further requests for repairs or credits - *Closing Date:* *Friday* Under this option, we would purchase the property as-is for *$2,525,000*, waive any further requests for repairs or credits, and close on Friday, provided the easement is removed. Option 3:Purchase price of *$2,450,000*, with the easement. We would not request any additional inspections, would purchase the home as-is, and would close on *Friday*

Subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] Insurance Quote - 5306 State Road 144, Greenwood, IN 46143
From: Sam <samgpresnal@gmail.com<mailto:samgpresnal@gmail.com>> Sent: Sunday, August 2, 2026 11:51 AM To: Leslie Appel Maher <LAppel@gregoryappel.com<mailto:LAppel@gregoryappel.com>> Cc: Jessica Eye <JEye@gregoryappel.com<mailto:JEye@gregoryappel.com>> Subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] Insurance Quote - 5306 State Road 144, Greenwood, IN 46143 Good morning Leslie, The sellers got back to me. Below is there response to the claims. -------- Claims: 1. The 25K claim was because of a few bats that found their way into our attic. The claim paid to have all attic entry points to be sealed thus preventing any further "bat infestations". Bats are a protected and they require special care to remove them and prevent further entry. In addition to the work needed to seal the attic, the money was used to also remove any and all bat waste/insulation, disinfect and re-insulate areas affected in the attic. This was done in 9/2024, and we have had no further issues. 2. One of the water claims was actually not a claim at all, but one was due to the fact I called after hours with a question which triggered a claim to be created. Apparently if you call with questions during the day, you are forwarded to your agency where the questions are answered in an appropriate manner. If you happen to call the general number after work hours as soon as the phone is picked up, a claim is created automatically. Obviously, I had no idea this was the process as I have never had a claim prior. The reason I called back in 2021 is because we found a dried water stain below the master bathroom. We had lived in the home for about a year prior to the stain being noticed. It was not wet but I called to see if I needed to notify my insurance company of what we found so it could be documented for the future. This led to the "water claim" being filed. The next morning the claims adjusted called, and I realized a claim had actually been created without them telling me. I told the claims adjuster the same info I did to the person the night before, and the claim was closed. We later found out from the prior owners one of the children overflowed the shower one time leading to the staining and no further water issues have been noticed since. Just in case we professionally sealed the base to ensure there would be no future risks. 3. The 2nd "water clam" in 2023 was triggered when a contracting company was hired to remove a retaining wall from the back yard, redirecting water drainage away from the downstairs patio and install a new retaining wall for a future pool. My insurance company suggested and strongly encouraged I create a claim in case something developed in relation to water damage to patio area so it could be documented appropriately by them and us. This documentation would be used in a court situation if needed. Luckly, we ended up getting a new contractor who was able to redirect water away in an appropriate manner, and we have had no further drainage concerns since. In the end, I requested the claim being closed, and a claims adjuster was never dispatched, and no payouts were received as noted.

To: Leslie Appel Maher
Cc: Jessica Eye
Subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] Insurance Quote - 5306 State Road 144, Greenwood, IN 46143<https://www.google.com/maps/search/5306+State+Road+144,+Greenwood,+IN+46143?entry=gmail&source=g>
From: Sam <samgpresnal@gmail.com<mailto:samgpresnal@gmail.com>> Sent: Sunday, August 2, 2026 11:51 AM To: Leslie Appel Maher <LAppel@gregoryappel.com<mailto:LAppel@gregoryappel.com>> Cc: Jessica Eye <JEye@gregoryappel.com<mailto:JEye@gregoryappel.com>> Subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] Insurance Quote - 5306 State Road 144, Greenwood, IN 46143<https://www.google.com/maps/search/5306+State+Road+144,+Greenwood,+IN+46143?entry=gmail&source=g> Good morning Leslie, The sellers got back to me. Below is there response to the claims. -------- Claims: 1. The 25K claim was because of a few bats that found their way into our attic. The claim paid to have all attic entry points to be sealed thus preventing any further "bat infestations". Bats are a protected and they require special care to remove them and prevent further entry. In addition to the work needed to seal the attic, the money was used to also remove any and all bat waste/insulation, disinfect and re-insulate areas affected in the attic. This was done in 9/2024, and we have had no further issues. 2. One of the water claims was actually not a claim at all, but one was due to the fact I called after hours with a question which triggered a claim to be created. Apparently if you call with questions during the day, you are forwarded to your agency where the questions are answered in an appropriate manner. If you happen to call the general number after work hours as soon as the phone is picked up, a claim is created automatically. Obviously, I had no idea this was the process as I have never had a claim prior. The reason I called back in 2021 is because we found a dried water stain below the master bathroom. We had lived in the home for about a year prior to the stain being noticed. It was not wet but I called to see if I needed to notify my insurance company of what we found so it could be documented for the future. This led to the "water claim" being filed. The next morning the claims adjusted called, and I realized a claim had actually been created without them telling me. I told the claims adjuster the same info I did to the person the night before, and the claim was closed. We later found out from the prior owners one of the children overflowed the shower one time leading to the staining and no further water issues have been noticed since. Just in case we professionally sealed the base to ensure there would be no future risks. 3. The 2nd "water clam" in 2023 was triggered when a contracting company was hired to remove a retaining wall from the back yard, redirecting water drainage away from the downstairs patio and install a new retaining wall for a future pool. My insurance company suggested and strongly encouraged I create a claim in case something developed in relation to water damage to patio area so it could be documented appropriately by them and us. This documentation would be used in a court situation if needed. Luckly, we ended up getting a new contractor who was able to redirect water away in an appropriate manner, and we have had no further drainage concerns since. In the end, I requested the claim being closed, and a claims adjuster was never dispatched, and no payouts were received as noted.

From: Sam <samgpresnal@gmail.com<mailto:samgpresnal@gmail.com>> Sent: Sunday, August 2, 2026 11:51 AM To: Leslie Appel Maher <LAppel@gregoryappel.com<mailto:LAppel@gregoryappel.com>> Cc: Jessica Eye <JEye@gregoryappel.com<mailto:JEye@gregoryappel.com>> Subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] Insurance Quote - 5306 State Road 144, Greenwood, IN 46143 Good morning Leslie, The sellers got back to me. Below is there response to the claims. -------- Claims: 1. The 25K claim was because of a few bats that found their way into our attic. The claim paid to have all attic entry points to be sealed thus preventing any further "bat infestations". Bats are a protected and they require special care to remove them and prevent further entry. In addition to the work needed to seal the attic, the money was used to also remove any and all bat waste/insulation, disinfect and re-insulate areas affected in the attic. This was done in 9/2024, and we have had no further issues. 2. One of the water claims was actually not a claim at all, but one was due to the fact I called after hours with a question which triggered a claim to be created. Apparently if you call with questions during the day, you are forwarded to your agency where the questions are answered in an appropriate manner. If you happen to call the general number after work hours as soon as the phone is picked up, a claim is created automatically. Obviously, I had no idea this was the process as I have never had a claim prior. The reason I called back in 2021 is because we found a dried water stain below the master bathroom. We had lived in the home for about a year prior to the stain being noticed. It was not wet but I called to see if I needed to notify my insurance company of what we found so it could be documented for the future. This led to the "water claim" being filed. The next morning the claims adjusted called, and I realized a claim had actually been created without them telling me. I told the claims adjuster the same info I did to the person the night before, and the claim was closed. We later found out from the prior owners one of the children overflowed the shower one time leading to the staining and no further water issues have been noticed since. Just in case we professionally sealed the base to ensure there would be no future risks. 3. The 2nd "water clam" in 2023 was triggered when a contracting company was hired to remove a retaining wall from the back yard, redirecting water drainage away from the downstairs patio and install a new retaining wall for a future pool. My insurance company suggested and strongly encouraged I create a claim in case something developed in relation to water damage to patio area so it could be documented appropriately by them and us. This documentation would be used in a court situation if needed. Luckly, we ended up getting a new contractor who was able to redirect water away in an appropriate manner, and we have had no further drainage concerns since. In the end, I requested the claim being closed, and a claims adjuster was never dispatched, and no payouts were received as noted.

Below is there response to the claims. -------- Claims: 1. The 25K claim was because of a few bats that found their way into our attic. The claim paid to have all attic entry points to be sealed thus preventing any further "bat infestations". Bats are a protected and they require special care to remove them and prevent further entry. In addition to the work needed to seal the attic, the money was used to also remove any and all bat waste/insulation, disinfect and re-insulate areas affected in the attic. This was done in 9/2024, and we have had no further issues. 2. One of the water claims was actually not a claim at all, but one was due to the fact I called after hours with a question which triggered a claim to be created. Apparently if you call with questions during the day, you are forwarded to your agency where the questions are answered in an appropriate manner. If you happen to call the general number after work hours as soon as the phone is picked up, a claim is created automatically. Obviously, I had no idea this was the process as I have never had a claim prior. The reason I called back in 2021 is because we found a dried water stain below the master bathroom. We had lived in the home for about a year prior to the stain being noticed. It was not wet but I called to see if I needed to notify my insurance company of what we found so it could be documented for the future. This led to the "water claim" being filed. The next morning the claims adjusted called, and I realized a claim had actually been created without them telling me. I told the claims adjuster the same info I did to the person the night before, and the claim was closed. We later found out from the prior owners one of the children overflowed the shower one time leading to the staining and no further water issues have been noticed since. Just in case we professionally sealed the base to ensure there would be no future risks. 3. The 2nd "water clam" in 2023 was triggered when a contracting company was hired to remove a retaining wall from the back yard, redirecting water drainage away from the downstairs patio and install a new retaining wall for a future pool. My insurance company suggested and strongly encouraged I create a claim in case something developed in relation to water damage to patio area so it could be documented appropriately by them and us. This documentation would be used in a court situation if needed. Luckly, we ended up getting a new contractor who was able to redirect water away in an appropriate manner, and we have had no further drainage concerns since. In the end, I requested the claim being closed, and a claims adjuster was never dispatched, and no payouts were received as noted.

Obviously, I had no idea this was the process as I have never had a claim prior. The reason I called back in 2021 is because we found a dried water stain below the master bathroom. We had lived in the home for about a year prior to the stain being noticed. It was not wet but I called to see if I needed to notify my insurance company of what we found so it could be documented for the future. This led to the "water claim" being filed. The next morning the claims adjusted called, and I realized a claim had actually been created without them telling me. I told the claims adjuster the same info I did to the person the night before, and the claim was closed. We later found out from the prior owners one of the children overflowed the shower one time leading to the staining and no further water issues have been noticed since. Just in case we professionally sealed the base to ensure there would be no future risks. 3. The 2nd "water clam" in 2023 was triggered when a contracting company was hired to remove a retaining wall from the back yard, redirecting water drainage away from the downstairs patio and install a new retaining wall for a future pool. My insurance company suggested and strongly encouraged I create a claim in case something developed in relation to water damage to patio area so it could be documented appropriately by them and us. This documentation would be used in a court situation if needed. Luckly, we ended up getting a new contractor who was able to redirect water away in an appropriate manner, and we have had no further drainage concerns since. In the end, I requested the claim being closed, and a claims adjuster was never dispatched, and no payouts were received as noted.

▶Derrick Hasenour → samgpresnal@gmail.com
From: Derrick Hasenour <derrickhasenour@gmail.com>To: "samgpresnal@gmail.com" <samgpresnal@gmail.com>
Good afternoon, I am glad we can finally communicate without "The Realtor" being stuck in the middle. I do not feel her presents was at all helpful in the transaction making it much more complicated that it really needed to be. If she had just provided us with your contact information, we could have bypassed a lot of miscommunications. Utilities List @ 5306 State Rd 144 and 5306 ½ State Rd 144 Greenwood, IN 46143 1. Electric — Johnson County REMC (JCREMC) Email: custservice@jcremc.com<mailto:custservice@jcremc.com> Phone: 317.736.6174 Hours: Monday-Friday 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Address: 750 International Dr. P.O. Box 309 Franklin, IN 46131 2. Water — Bargersville Utilities [long link omitted] 3. Fiber Internet — Johnson County Fiber (JCFiber) Residential Services 317-736-6174 Info@jcfiber.com<mailto:fiber@jcremc.com?subject=JCFiber%20Residential%20Services> 4. Trash and Recycling — Best Way Disposal 800-354-1830 Fax 317-270-5548 2577 Kentucky Avenue Indianapolis, IN 46221 5. Natural Gas — CenterPoint Energy https://www.citizensenergygroup.com/My-Account/Start-Stop-Transfer.aspx?Type=Start 6. Entry Gate Maintenance — K&K Fencing Address: 6520 Brookville Road Indianapolis, IN 46219 Phone: 317-463-5473 7. Cellular Service Gate Entry — DoorKing Inc Access Control Solutions since 1948 120 Glasgow Avenue, Inglewood, California 90301 U.S.A. Tel: 310-645-0023 FAX: 310-641-1586 We will leave all the information we have in relation to drawings of the home, lake, landscaping, and property in the laundry room when you come on 8/21/26. We will also leave keys and codes to the doors, front door, keycodes, garage doors, gate, and barn. The gate phone number to open and close is 317-443-5921. Call 317-443-5921 and wait for the beep then use 4 to keep open and 3 to close. The gate code we will give you upon arrival. General Maintenance of Gate/common area The right side of the gate is yours to care for. I usually need to pull/spray weeds at least once a month. The grasses will need to be cut now and again once winter sets in. The gate openers need the gear boxes check for oil needs at least yearly, and all gate hinges need greased at least 2 times a year. The gate opener has a cellular connection and has a monthly service contract which will be billed thru DoorKing as above. The lights up the lane are on a timer which is hidden in the grass up at the edge of your property and the neighbors along with a large breaker box that provides power to the lights and gate. The timer is located just below, and it will need to be adjusted with season changes and daylight savings time changes. Lake The lake will need to have its usual algae treatment completed for the whole lake and then spot treated as appropriate. The lake will need dye added as well to reduce undergrowth late in the season. Please also make sure to watch out for and treat duck weed as needed because it quadruples in amount every 48hrs. The best treatment is fluoride based and costs around $200 an ounce or so but works very very well. The fountain will need to be removed before the first freeze and cleaned. The pump must be stored in a water/antifreeze solution in a place where it won't freeze. The circuit can then be shut off at the breaker box. Barn: Make sure to plug up the heat tapes as soon as the freezing weather sets in or pipes will freeze in the barn and bathroom. The key code are the same as the home. You will want to purchase 2 dehumidifiers to keep running all the time to reduce moister and condensation. This keeps the fans from dropping and rust reduction. Make sure to always treat mice or consider a cat. Raccoons also like to dig their way under the back side of the barn so might need traps or just monitor closely to keep them out. Furniture you asked about along with pricing. 1. Beach Manufacturing Pool table w/ sticks and caddy and rug plus bar stools in downstairs kitchen area for free along with purchase. — $2500 2. 3 Outdoor couches and 2 glass top side tables -- $300 3. 4 Loungers with cushions and 2 glass top side tables -- $300 If you have any further questions please feel free to ask. Derrick and Sarah Derrick 317-292-1883 Sarah 317-292-1884

We had lived in the home for about a year prior to the stain being noticed. It was not wet but I called to see if I needed to notify my insurance company of what we found so it could be documented for the future. This led to the "water claim" being filed. The next morning the claims adjusted called, and I realized a claim had actually been created without them telling me. I told the claims adjuster the same info I did to the person the night before, and the claim was closed. We later found out from the prior owners one of the children overflowed the shower one time leading to the staining and no further water issues have been noticed since. Just in case we professionally sealed the base to ensure there would be no future risks. 3. The 2nd "water clam" in 2023 was triggered when a contracting company was hired to remove a retaining wall from the back yard, redirecting water drainage away from the downstairs patio and install a new retaining wall for a future pool. My insurance company suggested and strongly encouraged I create a claim in case something developed in relation to water damage to patio area so it could be documented appropriately by them and us. This documentation would be used in a court situation if needed. Luckly, we ended up getting a new contractor who was able to redirect water away in an appropriate manner, and we have had no further drainage concerns since. In the end, I requested the claim being closed, and a claims adjuster was never dispatched, and no payouts were received as noted.

Good afternoon Garrett, We’ve been asked to sign an amended easement agreement concerning the existing ingress and egress easements that provide access to our neighbors at 5306. Could you please review the agreement and advise us on how you recommend we proceed? Based on my read-through it seems everything works as we previously understood it, but the document adds specifics for maintenance. Additionally, there seems to be one small update to the easement. Previously, it stated, *'This driveway easement shall be constructed and maintained at the sole cost of Grantees'. *I don't think this makes a particularly big difference to us since splitting maintenance equally seems fair, but I wanted to point it out. Thanks! Sam & Regina

▶Darcy Knott → SamCc: Garrett Lawton, Regina Gray
From: Darcy Knott <darcy@truebloodre.com>To: Sam <samgpresnal@gmail.com>Cc: Garrett Lawton <glawton@mcneelylaw.com>, Regina Gray <graylregina@gmail.com>
Good morning! Just sending further information from the other realtor: Hi Darcy Yes , all neighbors knew/ know of this document and we are not pending. Rachel Freitas and I have Dr. Norris's home for sale at 5352 St Rd 144. When I had preliminary Title Work done the Attorney at the Title Company said that it is necessary to further define the relationship ( between the 3 owners ) that utilize the gate and shared drive at the entry. It is my understanding that each homeowner has been putting in approx $1000 a year to take care of the entry/gate etc.. I believe that this neighborly arrangement was by handshake. I have used Transantion Title ( for decades ) and the Attorney Tim Warner recommended this. He found that the HOA did not sign off on the original Grant of Easement so he created this amendment. This will benefit all 3 owners. I completely understand that they will want their attorney to review. Norris and Fletcher have agreed to sign. Hopefully we can move this forward as soon as possible. Garrett, please just let us all know what you think. Obviously an agreement was already there but this sounds/looks like they just want it tightened up a bit! Thanks Darcy

Hi John, Regina, and Sam I had a conversation with John and wanted to get us all on an email so we can communicate and come to a resolution ( hopefully ) that everyone will be ok with. We have heard Hassenhours thoughts that damage was done to the road during the construction of John's house, approx 2017. I believe that 5306 was built in 2001, that makes the main portion of the drive 25 years old. I have zero clue if the road was ever improved/ sealcoated etc.. in that time period. Fletcher only uses a small part of the drive, and John uses the part up to his entry ( and the portion that crosses land owned by Sam and Regina). and John has shared that Hassenhour was " running a business " out of the barn in the back. I guess you all need to have a discussion as to where you believe this issue is, ( or if there is actually an issue)and can it be dealt with easily. I dont want to be an arbitrator in this - but I'll try. ( I am not an attorney.) Regina and Sam What is the issue , what would you propose needs to be remedied and how ? I dont know what happened between John and The Hassenhours to challenge their relationship ? But hopefully we can " get your neighborly relationship started off on the right foot ". And of course, John hopes to sell his place soon ( which we are working on ). I will use the word " hopeful " again, hopefully we will have a new neighbor to introduce you to soon. I will also send you all the docs on these properties that have been recorded in Johnson County, ( at least the ones I have been given by John ). Please confirm receipt. Sincerely Dean Hicks Fletcher is just waiting to find out the status ( I believe the Fletchers are ready to move forward with revised amendment ) Once we have progress I will loop them in. CC: Freitas

So we felt it made sense to get the common road back to square one before signing a new easement agreement. Again, this is a lot of second hand and third hand information but that is the story to the best of our knowledge. Thanks Luke

These claims have an interesting back story that ended up causing us to switch insurance companies. Claims 1. The 25K claim was because of a few bats that found their way into our attic. The claim paid to have all attic entry points to be sealed thus preventing any further "bat infestations". Bats are a protected and they require special care to remove them and prevent further entry. In addition to the work needed to seal the attic, the money was used to also remove any and all bat waste/insulation, disinfect and re-insulate areas affected in the attic. This was done in 9/2024, and we have had no further issues. 2. One of the water claims was actually not a claim at all, but one was due to the fact I called after hours with a question which triggered a claim to be created. Apparently if you call with questions during the day, you are forwarded to your agency where the questions are answered in an appropriate manner. If you happen to call the general number after work hours as soon as the phone is picked up, a claim is created automatically. Obviously, I had no idea this was the process as I have never had a claim prior. The reason I called back in 2021 is because we found a dried water stain below the master bathroom. We had lived in the home for about a year prior to the stain being noticed. It was not wet but I called to see if I needed to notify my insurance company of what we found so it could be documented for the future. This led to the "water claim" being filed. The next morning the claims adjusted called, and I realized a claim had actually been created without them telling me. I told the claims adjuster the same info I did to the person the night before, and the claim was closed. We later found out from the prior owners one of the children overflowed the shower one time leading to the staining and no further water issues have been noticed since. Just in case we professionally sealed the base to ensure there would be no future risks. 3. The 2nd "water clam" in 2023 was triggered when a contracting company was hired to remove a retaining wall from the back yard, redirecting water drainage away from the downstairs patio and install a new retaining wall for a future pool. My insurance company suggested and strongly encouraged I create a claim in case something developed in relation to water damage to patio area so it could be documented appropriately by them and us. This documentation would be used in a court situation if needed. Luckly, we ended up getting a new contractor who was able to redirect water away in an appropriate manner, and we have had no further drainage concerns since. In the end, I requested the claim being closed, and a claims adjuster was never dispatched, and no payouts were received as noted. Derrick and Sarah Hasenour ------------------------------
